pr.title: Show the repository inbox in the panel and the console, and teach agents to use it
pr.head: db2d800f84785bfa8cfa1c8c9b7a6bfab726f356

summary: Projector keeps questions and requests for a person in an inbox. Earlier layers add a second inbox shared by that person’s sessions in one repository: another person’s agent can post there, and encrypted relay records carry answers back. This layer puts those repository entries beside the session’s own items in the Claude Code panel and terminal console.

A button on a peer’s question or request records the person’s response immediately with --as user. It sends no answer notification to the local session’s agent. Discuss instead quotes the entry so the person can ask that agent what to say. The messaging skill explains when an agent may post or answer, and the project plan records completion while leaving the two-person manual exercise for after merge.

cards.title: Two inboxes, separate delivery
cards.html:
• Session item: a question, request, notice, or message belonging to one agent session, identified by a numeric reference such as 1.
  • Repository entry: an incoming peer item, a copy of an item sent to a peer, or a peer’s reply, identified by r1.
  • Mirror: local files containing repository entries opened by the relay.

cards.title: Review at this head
cards.html:
• All three earlier panel findings remain fixed: entries render alone, snoozed entries return at their deadline, and peer Discuss quotes cannot answer local items.
  • This full follow-up checks integration with the daemon-only panel. The test harness now supplies subscription files and daemon cache results; the peer-only and hidden-snooze cases explicitly start with no subscriptions.
  • The configured exact-head gate passes the adapted regression tests and type checking. The two-person end-to-end exercise remains deferred.

groups.title: Separate repository entries from session items
groups.kicker: Types and commands distinguish peer responses from local answer delivery.
intro: Repository entries share an inbox listing with session items but have different ownership and delivery. The panel now recognizes their scope: "repo" tag and keeps them in a separate state list. Shared Python helpers let the CLI and console find the session’s registered repository and queue an encrypted response through the same core.

files.note: Defines the repository entry shape and the panel state that holds it.
Finds the repository mirror and builds commands for entry buttons.

checks.text: The entry command tests passed: incoming responses include --as user, while sent-entry actions do not impersonate a peer response.
The parser tests verify that r-reference quotes produce no local answer, request outcome, reply, or unclear mark, even with a prior drawer proposal or beside local quotes in either order.

files.note: Moves repository lookup and key resolution into shared helpers and adds console response adapters.
Uses those shared helpers, includes the listed repository in JSON, and supplies daemon startup to the console.

groups.title: Show peer entries in the Claude Code panel
groups.kicker: Mirror changes load entries, and each role gets its own drawer and buttons.
intro: The panel reads the repository from the session registration and watches the mirror beside the session’s item directory. An entry drawer shows peer text and related replies. Answer, Done, and Decline run commands directly; Discuss fills the prompt instead of answering through the local agent.

Repository entries count as panel content even when no pull request or local item is visible. The panel uses each entry’s snooze deadline and its own clock, and the quote parser keeps repository references in a separate namespace. New entries and expired snoozes also reopen a hidden panel.

The new base reads pull requests only from the watch daemon’s subscriptions and cache. The tests now use those files instead of legacy watcher fixtures. A session with no pull request subscriptions still polls its inbox, so peer entries can open its panel.

files.note: Loads and renders repository entries and dispatches their actions.

checks.text: The empty-panel condition counts repository entries. The adapted peer-only test starts with no subscriptions, confirms that new entries open the hidden panel, and draws those entries without a local item or pull request row.
Snooze filtering evaluates snoozed_until against the panel clock. Expiry invalidates the cached list and the tick reopens a hidden panel; shown and hidden expiry tests cover both paths.
Discuss retains the r-reference quote namespace. The adapted panel test submits Yes under a peer question and confirms that no local answer, outcome, decline, or unclear command runs.

files.note: Checks mirror paths, registration parsing, and the identity attached to entry commands.
Adds a repository entry harness and checks role display, sent replies, and direct user responses.

checks.text: The configured exact-head gate passes all 255 hook tests, including the adapted peer-only panel, shown/hidden snooze expiry, same-subject Discuss, and mixed-reference parser cases.

groups.title: Offer repository entry actions in the terminal console
groups.kicker: Each session’s panel reads the shared repository inbox.
intro: The terminal console now appends repository entries after a session’s pull requests and local items. Its drawers show peer details, replies, and role-specific controls. Responses use the shared repository helpers and start the daemon afterward so queued records can leave the machine.
A console Discuss action creates a message for the viewed session that quotes the peer entry. It does not fabricate an answer event on a session item.

files.note: Loads entries for each registered session, renders drawers, and handles response, snooze, close, reopen, and Discuss actions.
Covers entry display, user response identity, absence of local answer delivery, and replies on sent items.

checks.text: The original full review passed 243 focused Python tests covering console, inbox, peers, packaging, and permissions. This head leaves the console implementation and its tests unchanged.
The previous configuration-integration review passed 94 focused console and peer tests. This head leaves the console, repository-inbox helpers, and their configuration interface unchanged.

groups.title: Explain peer authority and record the project outcome
groups.kicker: Skills route peer replies to the main conversation and require the user’s instruction.
intro: A peer’s message is another person’s input, so it cannot authorize work for the user. The messaging skill now describes that boundary for repository inbox entries: the user chooses peers and directs posting and answering, while an agent reads a full reply before weighing it within the existing task.

The review and fix skills keep peer reply notifications in the main conversation. The CLI documentation describes the new controls, and the plan records how the three layers meet the acceptance criteria while deferring a two-person manual check.
